question: Should Microsoft Teams adopt this `accounts`/`defaultAccount` model, including root-setting inheritance and legacy single-bot compatibility, as its supported public multi-bot contract?
rationale: The implementation is technically coherent and well-proven, but this PR creates a broad configuration, setup, credential, routing, and persistent-state contract whose permanent semantics require channel-owner approval.

options.title: Approve the account contract
options.body: Accept the proposed inheritance and compatibility model, refresh the branch onto current `main`, and land after exact-merge proof.

options.title: Narrow the contract first
options.body: Keep the PR open while maintainers specify different identity requirements, inheritance rules, setup behavior, or state boundaries.

options.title: Decline core multi-account Teams
options.body: Close the implementation and retain one Teams bot identity per gateway if maintainers do not want this operational surface.

recommendation.title: Approve the account contract
recommendation.body: Accept the proposed inheritance and compatibility model, refresh the branch onto current `main`, and land after exact-merge proof.
